anomalies.obs: On the 'MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS' sheet, the gate-pull resistor R5 (10 kΩ) of the main-pump N-MOSFET T2 (IRLR2905) is tied to +3V3, so the gate is pulled HIGH whenever the pre-driver T1 is off and the ESP32 pin is high-impedance. The structurally identical ATO-valve driver uses R12 (10 kΩ) tied to GND (pull-DOWN) on T5's gate.
anomalies.expected: A low-side N-MOSFET pump switch must default OFF; its gate should be pulled down to GND (as the ATO valve correctly does with R12), not up to +3V3. The spec describes T2 as a 24 V main-circulation-pump low-side switch driven through R1/T1, with no intent for an active-high default-on pull-up.

evidence.quote: Main Pump block: '+3V3' arrow -> R5 10k -> T2 (IRLR2905) gate node shared with R1 100Ω and T1 collector
ATO Valve block: T5 (AON3400A) gate node -> R12 10k -> GND (pull-down)
T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) Main circulation-pump low-side switch ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) ... pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter)

anomalies.impact: During power-on / reset / before the firmware configures IO10, the ESP32 pin is floating, so R5 biases T2's gate to +3V3 and the main circulation pump runs unattended (default-ON), the opposite of the intended default-OFF and of the ATO valve's behaviour; this can run the pump dry or overflow the system and is inconsistent between the two otherwise-identical drivers.

parsed.summary: The schematic is largely consistent with the OPNhydro-r2 spec, but the main-pump gate-pull resistor R5 is tied to +3V3 instead of GND (the ATO-valve twin correctly uses R12 to GND), leaving the IRLR2905 default-ON whenever the MCU pin is high-impedance — a deviation from the intended default-OFF low-side pump switch.
